bolivia/la-paz-cable-car.name: Mi Teleferico cable cars
bolivia/la-paz-cable-car.description: A network of cable cars linking La Paz and El Alto, with views of the city and Illimani.
bolivia/la-paz-cable-car.details: The Teleferico is both public transport and a sightseeing ride. Lines cross the canyon of La Paz and rise to El Alto, with views of the city and the Illimani peak. A ride over the neighbourhoods is a good way to orient yourself on the first day. It is cheap and avoids steep streets, which are tiring at altitude.

bolivia/witches-market.name: Witches Market and Calle Jaen
bolivia/witches-market.description: Streets of herbs, amulets and dried llama foetuses beside the San Francisco church.
bolivia/witches-market.details: The Mercado de las Brujas sells herbs, charms and offerings used in Aymara rituals, and nearby Calle Jaen is a preserved colonial street with small museums. The San Francisco church and plaza are close. Ask before photographing vendors. Walk slowly, as La Paz is at 3,600 metres.

bolivia/valley-of-the-moon.name: Valley of the Moon
bolivia/valley-of-the-moon.description: A strange landscape of eroded clay pinnacles on the edge of La Paz.
bolivia/valley-of-the-moon.details: The Valle de la Luna is a maze of spires and canyons carved by wind and rain, with short footpaths of about forty minutes. It is a half-day trip from the city centre by taxi or tour. Bring a sun hat and water, because the altitude means strong sun.

bolivia/tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku archaeological site
bolivia/tiwanaku.description: The ruins of a pre-Inca civilisation, including the Gate of the Sun, a UNESCO site.
bolivia/tiwanaku.details: Tiwanaku was the capital of a culture that flourished before the Incas, about an hour and a half from La Paz. The Gate of the Sun, the Akapana pyramid and monolithic statues are the highlights. A guide helps make sense of the stone structures, and the nearby museums display the finds.

bolivia/death-road.name: Death Road (Camino de las Yungas) by bike
bolivia/death-road.description: A downhill ride on a former narrow cliff road from the Andes towards the Amazon.
bolivia/death-road.details: The North Yungas Road drops about 3,500 metres from the mountains to the subtropical valleys. Guided downhill rides provide bikes, helmets and a support van. Safety standards vary, so choose a reputable operator. Dress in layers, as temperatures change a lot on the descent. A serious but popular adventure.

bolivia/copacabana-isla-del-sol.name: Copacabana and Isla del Sol
bolivia/copacabana-isla-del-sol.description: A Lake Titicaca town and a sacred island of Inca ruins and walking paths.
bolivia/copacabana-isla-del-sol.details: Copacabana is a pilgrimage town on the lake, with a cathedral and a waterfront. Boats cross in about ninety minutes to Isla del Sol, the legendary birthplace of the Inca sun, with a ridge walk between the north and south ends, villages and terraces. Pack for altitude and cold evenings.

bolivia/uyuni-salt-flat.name: Salar de Uyuni
bolivia/uyuni-salt-flat.description: The largest salt flat on earth, with mirror-like reflections in the wet season and hexagon crusts in the dry season.
bolivia/uyuni-salt-flat.details: The Salar de Uyuni covers about 10,000 square kilometres, with the Isla Incahuasi cactus island and dazzling white horizons. Tours run as a day trip or on a multi-day jeep route to lagoons. From January to March a thin layer of water makes the ground a mirror, while the dry season gives access to more of the flats. Sunglasses and sun cream are essential.

bolivia/train-cemetery.name: Train Cemetery, Uyuni
bolivia/train-cemetery.description: Rusting steam locomotives abandoned on the edge of Uyuni town.
bolivia/train-cemetery.details: Just outside the town are the remains of trains from the era when minerals were shipped to the Pacific. The rusted engines are a favourite photograph at sunset or sunrise. It is a short stop that is usually combined with a salt flat tour.

bolivia/sunset-salt-flat.name: Salt flat sunrise or sunset
bolivia/sunset-salt-flat.description: A guided evening or dawn on the flats, when the light changes the colours.
bolivia/sunset-salt-flat.details: Sunset and sunrise turn the white plain pink and gold and give the best reflections. Operators offer a short tour to the flats for the light, often with a drink toasting the sunset. Dress warmly, because it is very cold after dark, even in summer.

bolivia/sucre-white-city.name: Sucre, the white city
bolivia/sucre-white-city.description: A UNESCO colonial city of whitewashed buildings, plazas and museums at a gentler altitude.
bolivia/sucre-white-city.details: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, with a pleasant climate and a compact centre. The Casa de la Libertad museum tells the story of independence, and the plaza is lined with cafes. The Recoleta viewpoint looks over the red roofs. Chocolate is a local speciality.

bolivia/tarabuco-dinosaur.name: Dinosaur footprints and Tarabuco market
bolivia/tarabuco-dinosaur.description: Cretaceous footprints on a wall near Sucre and a Sunday market in a traditional town.
bolivia/tarabuco-dinosaur.details: Cal Orck'o has a vertical wall with thousands of dinosaur footprints, and a park with models. The Sunday market in Tarabuco is a highlight, where Yampara people sell textiles in traditional dress. Check the days, as the market is held only on Sundays.

bolivia/potosi-cerro-rico.name: Potosi and the Cerro Rico mines
bolivia/potosi-cerro-rico.description: A high-altitude silver-mining city and tours of working cooperative mines.
bolivia/potosi-cerro-rico.details: Potosi was once among the richest cities in the world from the silver of Cerro Rico. Guided tours enter the working mines, where miners labour in poor conditions, and visitors give coca leaves and gifts. The tours are cramped, dusty and at 4,000 metres altitude, so they are not suitable for people with heart or breathing problems. The Casa de la Moneda mint museum is a good non-mine option.

bolivia/lagunas-altiplano.name: Altiplano lagoons and Laguna Colorada
bolivia/lagunas-altiplano.description: Red and green lakes, flamingos and geysers on a multi-day jeep route south of Uyuni.
bolivia/lagunas-altiplano.details: The Reserva Eduardo Avaroa has Laguna Colorada, coloured red by algae, Laguna Verde, geysers and hot springs, at over 4,000 metres. The jeep route usually takes two or three days with basic lodges. Nights are very cold. This is the highlight of longer Uyuni tours.
